primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Mistaken identity is one of the enumerated non-conviction grounds, and relief runs on the same free petition vehicle as the other non-conviction grounds, with an added factual showing that the person was arrested or charged because of a case of mistaken identity.
The chapter-wide definitions section, which defines mistaken identity for the whole chapter.
The court forwards the order to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation within 30 days of entry.
Expunction restores the person, in contemplation of law, to the status occupied before arrest, indictment, information, trial and conviction.

counselFlags: Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it.

No official Tennessee participant form exists. Both state form indices were inspected directly and neither publishes an expunction form of any kind; this is a negative finding established from the authoritative index, not a failure to search. A controlled custom instrument is therefore the only available strategy, and it is not represented as an official form.

Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025 and codified by Public Chapter 608 effective 2026-03-25, and clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering — the state's own expunction page still reasons from a section that has been nothing but definitions since 2025-04-24. A petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet carries the current citation and instructs the participant to confirm it with the clerk or the district attorney general before filing.
Tennessee expunction reaches no federal, military, tribal or out-of-state record, and a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on a clearance check.

The governing section prescribes no caption form and no contents for the participant's instrument. The caption follows the ordinary criminal-case style of the court having jurisdiction, with the filer designated as the source designates them. What individual clerks and courts in fact expect is not established and no county practice was surveyed; the caption is a visual- and counsel-review item.
This route is free: mistaken identity is one of the non-conviction grounds and those records must be removed and destroyed without cost to the person.
What evidence Tennessee courts accept as establishing mistaken identity is not established. The packet prompts for the participant's own account and documents and specifies no proof standard.

Under the pre-reorganization numbering a petitioner could provide evidence of the circumstances and request an expedited order, on which finding the court was to direct the bureau and any other expunging entity to act in an expedited manner. Whether that expedited-order duty survived the reorganization in the same terms was not established, and it is not asserted. The expedited request is carried as a conditional component that states the participant's request without asserting the duty.
Any dispute about whether the participant is in fact the person arrested or charged is a factual contest and is outside self-help.

The state control number is a manual-completion item read from the participant's own criminal history. It stays a bracket in generated output; the order cannot be completed without it, and the participant is told to capture it early.

The shared renderer's fixed section heading "VI. VERIFICATION" is a Pennsylvania-derived artefact of the frozen renderer contract, not a Tennessee drafting choice. Nothing in the governing section requires verification. This is a visual- and counsel-review item.
No fee figure is quoted anywhere in this packet. The source records no retrievable amount, and the filing-fee field is left null rather than filled with a circulating number.
No fee-waiver instrument is included and the fee-waiver field is left null, because the source establishes no waiver mechanism for this route.
The governing section states no waiting period. None is pleaded, none is imported from a neighbouring section, and the waiting-period field is left null.

Notarization is not prescribed by the governing section and no verification statute exists to cite, so verificationStatute.citation is left null and the signature block carries no penalty citation. County practice may differ, and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk.

Self-help stop conditions: Any dispute with the district attorney general about eligibility, or any indication the office will oppose. Any other conviction anywhere on the record, including federal and out-of-state convictions that would be ineligible in Tennessee. Unpaid court costs, fines or restitution, which mean the sentence is not complete. Any DUI, sexual offence or registration matter. Any domestic violence or child-victim offence. Federal, military, tribal or out-of-state records, which Tennessee expunction does not reach. Immigration consequences, and any security-clearance question. Any question that turns on whether the county clerk uses the pre-2025 or the reorganized section numbering. Any dispute about whether the participant is in fact the person arrested or charged. Proving mistaken identity is a factual showing, and a contested one is outside self-help. The participant cannot document the circumstances at all.

provenance.registryExcerpt: Mistaken identity is one of the enumerated non-conviction grounds in the reorganized § 40-32-106(a)(1), and Public Chapter 268 of 2025 rewrote § 40-32-101 as a chapter-wide definitions section that defines mistaken identity for the whole chapter. Relief runs on the same free petition vehicle as the other non-conviction grounds, with an added factual showing that the person was arrested or charged because of a case of mistaken identity. The pre-reorganization provision the controlling review cited, former § 40-32-101(a)(1)(C)(i), also allowed the petitioner to provide evidence of the circumstances and request that the court order the expunction be expedited, on which finding the court was to order the TBI and any other expunging entity to act in an expedited manner. Whether that expedited-order duty survived the reorganization in the same terms was not established from an official source on 2026-08-06, and it is not asserted here. Venue: Statewide statute with originating-court venue. The petition goes to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action — the county criminal, circuit or general sessions court where the case originated. A person with cases in several counties files separately in each. There is no statewide participant form, so what varies locally is the clerk's own paperwork: the AOC directs filers to check with the court clerk because separate forms may be required for multiple charges. Destination: The county criminal, circuit or general sessions court having jurisdiction in the previous action — Confirmed on 2026-08-06 by direct inspection of both Tennessee AOC form indices: the self-help forms page publishes only divorce and order-of-protection forms, and the full forms-and-publications inventory covers appellate, divorce, general sessions civil, mediation, non-IV-D child support, order of protection, parenting plan and trial court forms, plus licensing forms. No expunction form appears in either. This is a negative finding established by inspection of the authoritative index, not by failure to search. filing: A petition to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action, filed with that court's clerk. fees: None. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing. Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it. No reach to federal records; a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on clearance checks. Exclusion: Any case where the participant was in fact the person arrested or charged. Exclusion: Any case where the participant's information is on the record for a reason other than mistaken identity, which routes to the ordinary non-conviction grounds. Exclusion: Any dispute about identity, which is a factual contest rather than a showing. Waiting period — Statutory waiting period: None. Waiting period — TBI transmission: The court sends the order to the TBI within 30 days of entry.
